title: Students and professors
concept: Translating 'six times as many students as professors' into S = 6P, and testing equations with real numbers.
kept: The sentence and the S/P equation question
The two candidate equations S = 6P and 6S = P
The common mistake of following word order (6S = P)
Showing why by putting in numbers (2 professors, 12 students) and checking both equations
filled_in: Order of activity: guess, add students (6 per professor), test each equation, explanation notes, slider, takeaway
Simple picture: orange circles for professors, blue circles for students
Slider for 1 to 6 professors as the explore step
Guess feedback compares the guess to the equation that passes the test
math_check: Students are drawn as 6 circles per professor and S and P are counted from the drawn circles. Each table row computes both sides from those counts: S vs 6*P (12 vs 12, equal) and 6*S vs P (72 vs 2, not equal). Checked by hand for P=1..6: S=6P holds, 6S=P never does (6S is at least 36 times P). The automated check passed with no problems or warnings.
